utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that his beating occurred in front of the administrative, or what you call the central building, where he was waiting to go in for interrogation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The cause for the beating, according to what you said, was the word he used "Bujrum," addressed to one of the guards who was eating.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we come from the same parts and we are familiar with words of Turkish origin, and we know what it means and you explained, in answer to the question of His Honour Judge Riad, you said that it meant "Help yourself" or "You're welcome to join in." Mr. Rizo Hadzalic wasn't eating. How did he use this word of Turkish origin, meaning "Join me in my meal"?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said -- when people eat in our part of the country, you know that you're very well because as you just said we come from the same parts. It is customary, if you or I am eating, you offer food to someone standing and watching. And he was meant -- what he meant was because he was eating that he should have said "Bujrum." He perhaps expected the guard to offer him some food, to join him in his meal. And then what happened happened. You know that these words of Turkish origin were not used only by Muslims; there were quite a number of Serbs using it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. That's what I meant. You personally watched this beating up.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you two or three more brief questions.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only two or three?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Oklopcic, do you know who was responsible for organising the food, such as it was, in the camp?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know to whom the investigators were answerable?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You mean those who questioned -- interrogated the prisoners? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, or rather within the security services or in general, were there members who used to work in the Omarska company?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the mine, among the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. No, among the people working in the security service.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. I know people who worked in the school. Yes, there were people who used to work there. Yes, that is correct. I see what you're asking me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me make myself quite clear. Within the framework of the organisation, such as it existed, there were a certain number of persons who were employed in the Omarska mine.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean during the period when it was a camp?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Who was their superior?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Oklopcic, I have no further questions, and I hope you will be able to return home as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope you will go home, too, soon. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have finished my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Simic. Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Before the next counsel starts his cross, can I just raise a matter to answer some of the issues raised by Mr. Simic, because I'm concerned they may come up again, and I'd like to clear the air. Could we do it in private session, please, turn off the public microphones?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're going into private session, then, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in public session, and you may commence. Please excuse me, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Oklopcic, I shall be as brief as possible and go through your statement, because you made some imprecise answers. I don't doubt the truth of them, your statements, but they were not just not precise enough. Tell us what happened on the 30th of May, 1992. With respect to that, your statement in the examination-in-chief differs form -- your testimony in the examination-in-chief differs from your statement because you said the alleged attack.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The 30th of May. The 30th of May. It's clearer there. In the statement, you say that 70 to 150 people attacked a town full of Serb soldiers. You don't know why this happened, but they took over Radio Prijedor and that you joined them?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What that how it was?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did this attack exist or not?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You call it an attack, but I call it an attempt to liberate the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Very well. I accept that. Once again, there was a Professor Lukic, and he said that 90 per cent of the misunderstandings between us is the terms we use. So it existed?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down, please. The interpreters kindly request this.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some people taken prisoner and later on did you later see them in Omarska, from that attempt to liberate the town, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. A number of people were taken into custody, and I saw them during my stay in Omarska, and later on, if they were arrested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please make pauses in between questions and answers, otherwise, you can speak outside the courtroom, because I think you're here for us to understand you. But if you continue like that, you can go outside the courtroom, you can talk together, and we can do something else. So please think of us, not only the interpreters, but us Judges as well, and the court reporters as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were people taken prisoner, you saw some of them?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that some people were brought in later on, probably as the result of being caught.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, being caught later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you rank them among civilians, the civilian population, in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do include them among the civilian population, and I'll tell you the reasons for that. Those young men, there were about 100 of them, first of all did not receive weapons from the Yugoslav army or from the police. Therefore, they were civilians. How they came by these weapons, how they purchased the weapons, that is another question altogether. But the difference between the civilian and, let us say, the army peaks and police peaks was that the Serbian population had received weapons from the police forces and the Yugoslav forces. These young men who tried to liberate the town or to return the town, get the town back, as I say, had no weapons at all, and this turned out to be seen later on. But they had very poor weapons. They had pistols of some kind. That's why I say that I do rank them among the civilians, because it's a difference between the regular army and civilians who got their weapons -- came by weapons in some way and tried to liberate the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you'll agree with me that they were young male men with weapons who came by those weapons in an illegitimate way.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with you there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The checkpoint that existed at Hambarine, were those people armed there, the ones that manned it?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there. Probably they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they get their weapons in a regular fashion? Because you said it was the Territorial Defence, did you not?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said no. The Territorial Defence, when the town was taken over, all the weapons of the Territorial Defence was given to the hands of the Serbian population on the 30th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the word "Territorial Defence" cannot be used for people who were at the checkpoints in Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably not, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Asked by Mr. Keegan, you said that injured Serb soldiers said something in an interview on television or on the radio, whatever.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did state that. On Serbian television. I said that he spoke on Serbian television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what did he say?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that the patrol, there were four or five of them in the car, that they were attacked at that checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period of May 1992, that is to say, before that attempt at liberation, could you tell us, if you happen to recall, when did the first Muslim die?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first Muslim, when he died, you want to know. Well, he died in the Prijedor area, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Which means Kozarac and all the rest?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A distinguished citizen from Brezicani was killed. I think his name was Jusuf Kucukovic. And this happened, this occurred in the period before the attack or the liberation of Prijedor. What the date was exactly, I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Kozarac on the 25th? Did anything happen there?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Serb army attacked Kozarac, and a Muslim died, I assume there. Not one, many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean 25. I don't want to speak instead of you. I know exactly what happened, and that's why I said "some," which means more than one. Was this event before or after that?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The killing of Jusuf Kucukovic, that was before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about that Kucukovic in relation to Hambarine or can't you say?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It was before the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In your testimony, you mentioned a number of guards and names who were in Krkan's shift, and after Krkan's shift, so on and so forth. Now, I would like to know the following to clarify something about that individual and I can't ascertain who that individual is. You mentioned a certain person named -- I think he was a guard. His name was Pavlic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My first question: Is that his name or his nickname?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is his surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I meant, his surname.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's his surname, and his name was Milan. So Milan Pavlic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I then state that it wasn't Pavlovic or Popovic either?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you describe this man to us? Did he have any characteristic traits on his head or on his hair?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had a white strand. He had died his hair white, a strand of white hair here in front. Otherwise he had dark hair. He was a bit larger than me. I'm large, but he was even larger. And he was under the age of 30, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, coming to organisation in the Omarska camp. You spoke about the structure; I don't want to repeat that. Do you happen to know whether they were formally appointed? You worked in a school. You know what it means when somebody is formally, officially appointed. Were they officially appointed commander, deputy commander, shift commander, and so on? Were there any official appointments?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm just waiting for the Judge to understand what you're saying. My answer to that question is I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your source of information, then, that they were -- that -- beginning from Meakic, who is not here, and going on from there?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My source of information was my stay in the Omarska concentration camp. That is my answer, number 1. Number 2, it was what the guards said amongst themselves. They clearly talked about who the superior was in the concentration camp of Omarska. And number 3, all of us, and I say this in my statement, saw who the shifts reported to, who the shifts were handed on to, and so on. I say that I did not see a signature, but that is my opinion and I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a flag on a crooked pole and that there was a flag-raising ceremony. Could you describe who was present at this flag ceremony? Not the ordinary guards or somebody who had just come in to bring some food, but the people we're talking about now.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said, the flag was not raised at the beginning, and that is why we found it strange that suddenly, after a few days had gone by, that this flag was improvised. You know what improvisation means. It was placed underneath the tap. How and why, I don't know. When shifts were taken over, usually at 7.00 in the morning, give or take five minutes either way, the shift leader and the commander, whether it was Kvocka or Zeljko Meakic, but usually it was the shift leader who was present. Every time Kvocka and Meakic were not present, it was the shift leader. And you know, when I say "shift leader," what I mean. So not those who were in the hangars; they didn't have to attend the ceremony. It was us, we who were outside on the pista, we necessarily attended this ceremony. And as I said, sometimes they would make fun of the whole thing. We had to keep quiet. But why they did that, I can't explain to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what did they actually do? Not what you did. What did they do?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they would raise the flag, and that's all. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you listened to a hymn, some kind of music.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. I just had to sing the nationalistic songs when those people from Banja Luka or Prijedor would come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the flag ceremony?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing. There was no music during that ceremony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. No music. In the course of your stay there, you were there for --

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it is the 26th of June. I was a history teacher ten years ago, so I do remember that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on this day, Vidovdan? Anything specific?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very often, in the course of my stay, helicopters would descend, military transport helicopters, and we would be forced -- you know that black belt used for the mine, mining ore, we had to -- they cut -- that is to say, this belt was four metres long, approximately, and cut into sections, and it was two metres across, and we had to -- not all of us, but those of us who were selected had to load that belt onto the helicopter. And some fire was being made and this was used. But the guards themselves used to say that this belt was used to line transporters and tanks because the Zoljas, hand-held rocket launchers, couldn't hit a tank if it was lined with this. But was any -- was there firing on Petrovdan and Vidovdan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the guards from who were in Krkan's shift?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Krkan's shift, I don't think they were all directly from Omarska, but they were from Jelicka and areas like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Omarska and Jelicka.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were not from Maricka?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I call my shift -- My shift was from Maricka. That was the shift I knew very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Maricka shift is the one you mentioned most frequently with respect to Ecim.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was in respect to Ecim?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not with respect to Ecim. I mentioned Krkan's shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in your statement, that is what you say.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm quite sure I didn't say that. There might be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes, nobody is perfect.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not my fault that it was Krkan's shift that day. And I said that in respect to Hankin, that it was Maricka's shift and Bectr Medunjanin as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slavko Ecim was brought to the camp. It is page 17, paragraph 2 of your statement, and in English it is on page 23. The English version, page 23, the last -- no, page 22. The English version is page 22. "On the same day, when I was interrogated ..." I don't have to read it out. We're all literate here. But you go on to state, "I think that the guards in the group were from Maricka."

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, but -- I might have said it, but it wasn't that way. That is not how it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me one more thing, and I'll be finished in just a moment. To put something else right, did you receive bread for food?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the transcript, because that was omitted from the transcript yesterday.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We would receive a small piece of bread, but we did receive bread, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the water that you were talking about, is it the water that went through these pipes before the camp was made?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people drink it, then?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People probably did. I didn't work at Omarska, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it wasn't special water that came out of these taps?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just know that later on the guards didn't drink the water from the same taps that we drank from. Whether the water was poisoned or not, I never said that. I can't maintain that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This is too fast. This is much too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your stay, you saw Krkan. Could you tell us where you saw him?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the pista. He would go past the pista, and mostly, when we went upstairs to the central building up on the upper storey where the interrogations went on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see him anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did see him in other parts as well because he was there; not only him, but all the others who were in this leadership cadre, they would walk around the whole camp. But as I was on the pista throughout that time, I saw him on many occasions, and that is no secret that he would come there and walk past and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to see him in -- what shall I call this, this part, this glass part up here?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Lots of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was standing around and looking. And in the evening he would just have a white vest on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he stood and watched?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not have any weapons on some occasions, and on others he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any guard post there of any kind?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever happen to see him standing guard in that area?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I know what you're getting at. There's a film, you know. A film was filmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I know all about that, and that is not something that is contested. During your statement, you say at one point, if I heard you correctly during your testimony, and I apologise if I heard you incorrectly -- you said, "Brk was Meakic's right hand and his assistant." Who is Brk? What do you mean by "Brk"?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a young man whose nickname was Brk or moustache in translation. Wherever Meakic went, he went with him. They would drive the same vehicle. They would beat the same people, people who were caught at Ljubija. I think his surname was Tadic but I'm not sure. Anyway, his nickname was Brk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he belong to any forces? Was he the police, the army, or whatever?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he wore the uniform of a police reserve force. It was a blue uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you know what the role was of the late Simo Drljaca with respect to the camp? You needn't -- I don't mean then, I mean generally did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can I say an extra sentence? Well, I don't want to run away from the truth, I want people to understand. You probably know that I did know Simo Drljaca because he worked as a lawyer covering all 16 or 14 primary schools that existed in the Prijedor municipality. So we did know each other well. We would sit in at many meetings together, but I can also tell you that he was not capable as a jurist, and I don't think he ever won a case in court. And that is why I find it all the more strange how come Mr. Drljaca should occupy such a leadership post of that kind? Who had chosen him when he was incapable, as he was? And you also asked me what role he played. Well, he had a great role, that is my personal opinion. I think he had a great role to play. Whether he had somebody above him, a superior, I don't know. But I did know him exceptionally well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So with respect to the Omarska camp, he did have some authority?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More or less than Meakic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Greater competencies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention Hankin in your previous statement but you mention him here.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did. Why it was not introduced, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's an answer too. At one given point, you state something about Soskan during the examination-in-chief. You mentioned Soskan. I wasn't quite clear. Did you see him shoot or did you think that he did the shooting or did you hear that he did the shooting?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it. I saw him shoot but I'm not quite sure 100 per cent. I think, I think I said that I thought it was Soskan, but I am not certain. I saw a soldier firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're not 100 per cent certain that it is him.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I wasn't a 100 per cent sure and that is what I said in the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we've clarified that point which wasn't quite clear. You mentioned an individual named Timarac, Zeljko Timarac.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, what was he there?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't anything. He would just come into Omarska and abuse and kill people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a civilian?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wore a uniform. He had a uniform on, a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's why I'm asking. Yes, thank you. You mentioned weapons, the weapons of certain individuals, and then you said he had a pump-action rifle. The weapons that they had, those whom you say were commanders or shift leaders, or I didn't quite unless you, but was there any difference between them and the other guards?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they different?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Milojica Kos, for example, he didn't have a rifle, he just had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Krkan?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, when he was on the pista, he never carried an automatic rifle, but as you say, on one of the pictures he was carrying an automatic rifle. Miro Kvocka did not always have a pump-action gun with him, but he did have one. Zeljko Markovic had a pistol, sometimes he did not have any automatic weaponry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other guards? Did they have weapons at all times or did they not have them at times?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had weapons at all times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It never happened that a reserve guard or some one did not have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when he was having a rest and he would put it down beside him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes, but otherwise that's that. Finally, sir, you've gone through some bad times and seen some even worse things from your personal experience because some people fared worse than you. Do you feel any -- do you feel the need for revenge? Do you feel the urge for revenge of any kind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Mr. Fila. I see that Madam Hollis is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm just interrupting on behalf of the court reporter who is indicating that she's not getting any of this exchange. I wanted to perhaps have us slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's always the same question. You must make pauses between questions and answers. Otherwise, everything gets mixed up, you overlap each other. So please try and pay attention to that. We will be very grateful to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I like the fact that you said that you were sorry that the Serbs had been killed. I am also sorry that other people had been killed, Croats as well. They're neither yours nor mine, so we're sorry about them too.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have friends who are Serbs and Croats, but I'm a Macedonian which is something else again, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you feel any hatred towards a whole peoples or not? Do you feel the need for revenge of any kind? I'd like to hear your answer?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I thought that somebody might ask me that, and I don't want to say that I was ready for an answer. But you must understand that I do hate, but to do them what they did to my people, I would never do to them what they did to us. I hope that they will get proper justice in the eyes of God and before this Court as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you something else, towards the people. I hope you don't feel any hatred towards people. That's what I wanted to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're now going to hear Mr. Jovan Simic. Mr. Simic, you have the floor, if you please. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before beginning with the cross-examination, I should like to tender into evidence the Serbian version of a document compiled by the witness himself, and the English translation of the same, and the B/C/S version, marked 22nd of June, or rather the code of the country. It appears to have been made in 1995, which we didn't know. I apologise. I made an omission. The English version is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, but I think that we have here two documents. We have the translation of only one of the two, I don't know whether there is another. Mr. Dubuisson, we have two versions in English, do we?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document that I have in front of me is only in one version, in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I think that we have two B/C/S documents, a manuscript and another typed text, with the mark "22nd of June" in B/C/S, and we have the translation only of the manuscript. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the document written by hand and the document translated into English are one and the same document, in fact. The B/C/S version, with an English translation, that is how it was disclosed to us in the supporting material. Another document is a statement that Mr. Keegan said was marked 22nd June, and it represents the country in which it was given. We do not have an English version, nor did we ever receive it, and that is why we are tendering it in the original that was disclosed to us, that is, in the B/C/S language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see things are clearer now. Can the registrar give us the number of this exhibit so we can identify the document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document "22nd June", only in B/C/S, will be marked D2/5, and the other document for which we have an English translation will be D1/5, D1/5A for the English version, which is a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, we are now able to begin, and once we have the documents marked, it is easier to use the code, please. So you may begin, Mr. Simic. I think we are in a position to be able to do so. Cross-examined by Mr. J. Simic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Oklopcic, good day to you.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please take this list, marked D1/5, which is in fact a list of the most responsible people that you compiled by yourself, by hand. Did you write it?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this document consists of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. There's no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I have a question about the way these documents are marked. It says -- I heard D2/5 and D1/5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. O'Sullivan, excuse me, I wasn't able to follow you. I apologise. Could you repeat your remark?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. My question concerns the way these documents were marked. The numbering they received, I heard D1/5 and D2/5. If I'm mistaken, please correct me, but I believe that Prcac is the fifth accused and it should be D5/1 and D5/2, unless I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. O'Sullivan. Let us see with Mr. Dubuisson.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We no longer use that system. We use the slash and the number attributed to the accused last. For Kvocka, it was D24/1. In this case, it is D1/5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that clear now, Mr. O'Sullivan? Thank you. I apologise for interrupting you. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. Jovan Simic, I apologise once again. Please proceed. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Oklopcic, you compiled this list.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is having problems with the interpretation. He is not getting the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hear it now. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. It is probably our mistake. We found the English version of the document marked D2/5. So we haven't had the time to photocopy it, but we would like to tender it and we will photocopy it later, if we may.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Oklopcic, we will finally get going, I hope. So on this document, you made a list of the most responsible people.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guard leaders and guards, the inspectors and interrogators.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was able to remember at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people who were taken away and liquidated, who were exchanged, who were missing. And on page 4, you signed this document, saying that the names from 1 to 4 are truthful and authentic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you compile this list?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When in 1993?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was almost immediately after your release, so I assume your memory was best then.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: If you compiled such a list in December --

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In January, I'm sorry. In January. Why did you not mention then Dragoljub Prcac?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer your question. Dragoljub Prcac was someone I did not know personally, and I saw him least in the camp. At that time I would have forgotten many others. If somebody had mentioned the name at the time I was writing this list, I would have asked who that man was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that means that you acquired knowledge about Dragoljub Prcac later on.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had him in mind from the first day, like all the others. But Dragoljub Prcac, for me, was not as important at the time as the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was he not so important?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I would see Mr. Dragoljub Prcac only as one of the leaders in the camp. I didn't see him much anyway. He appeared later in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you see him as a leader of the camp?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the leaders. A commander of the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention him in your statement of December 1994.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention him in the statement that has just been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention him today when you were asked about who wore what kind of weapons.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's better that I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovan Simic, don't make assertions. Ask questions. Ask questions. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him often outside the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end. At first I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he move around most?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like all the others, in front of the central building, upstairs, downstairs, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he carry as a weapon?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Always?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not always. He had a pistol but sometimes he wore an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was dressed in military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The former SMB, or olive-grey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in connection with an event that you mentioned, would you please briefly, so as not to take too much time, can you tell us the date of that event, and then I will ask you about certain persons. You spoke about Nasic. I would like to know when, roughly, this occurred, not to the day but an approximation.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It was, I said that today and also the last time, it was seven or ten days after arrival in our camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were then at the pista, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When Mehmedalija Nasic was killed, I was in the central building, in the canteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Edin Crnalic present then? Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mirsad Alisic present?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Jasmir Okic present?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. I think they were. I'm not sure, but I think they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Hankin was killed --

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- when was that?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was two or three weeks in June, end of June. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Senad Ferhatovic present?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was. I know who you mean, but I mentioned those whom I could remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was (redacted) present?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Amir Mesic present?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Nedim Kapetanovic present?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Becir Medjunjanin was victimised, when was that? Was Anes Medjunjanin there and Mokic Fedul [phoen], Sead Cikota?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Abdulah Brkic? Do you know Abdulah Brkic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know now. Some time has gone by since then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Riza Hadzalic, you remember the event that you described. Was Ferhatovic present?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Hodzic present?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nusret Sivac? Edin Crnalic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mirsad Alisic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mirsada Hadzalic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirsada Hadzalic was not present. She was brought in later on, after her man, Riza Hadzalic, had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nusreta Sivac.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was in the camp but I don't know whether she was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Omer Mesanovic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fehim Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Abdulah Brkic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The case with Cifut Ramadanovic, when was that roughly?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in July. I think it was the beginning of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Besim Hodzic was present?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Besim Hodzic was almost always with his sons at the pista. I know these people you are listing extremely well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nedim Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One further question. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Jovan Simic. Mr. Tosic, how much time do you need, more or less?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the time for the break, our suggestion would be that we begin the cross-examination after the break. Maybe we could begin a couple of minutes earlier, because we certainly can't finish the cross in these couple of minutes that remain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for your suggestion. But I was asking how much time you need more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By the end of the working day, we will finish our cross-examination. I don't think we will go into the next day of hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But many of the questions have already been asked. Never mind. We shall have a half hour break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. We are resuming the hearing. Who is going to cross-examine, Mr. Tosic or Mr. Stojanovic? Either change your seats or the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on behalf of the Defence team of Zoran Zigic, my colleague Slobodan Stojanovic will be cross-examining the witness, so there's no need for us to change seats. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I beg your pardon. You may begin, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think it is a good idea for us to share out this truly difficult task. Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would prefer to discuss with you my favourite subjects, such as history and geography. Unfortunately, it is my duty to discuss with you something that I consider to be most unpleasant myself, but I'm sure it is even worse for you, but it is my duty as the Defence counsel to ask you about these things. On the first day of your testimony, you began with events in 1991, saying that already then your colleagues had started wearing JNA uniforms. In 1995 [sic], was the SFRY still the country of all the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned 1995. I think you made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I beg your pardon. 1991.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the country of all the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about 1991. According to the then constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did it clearly provide for the obligation of all citizens of that republic to defend the Yugoslavia of that day?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion you mentioned a number of times that on the 30th of April, 1992 -- we are talking about the first day of your testimony -- the Serb Crisis Staff took over power in Prijedor. Before that, shall we say from October 1991, was there another Crisis Staff in existence?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. An attempt was made to constitute what we could call a government of Prijedor municipality. On the basis of the results of the elections in 1991, the power was still shared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I then ask you, and I don't know whether this question was permitted or not, was this Crisis Staff composed exclusively of Muslims -- I can give you the composition, to remind the witness -- from October of 1991.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who was a member, if there was any such body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I remind you of that, then. Muhamed Cehajic was president; Mirsad Medjujavic [phoen], Mustafa Hodzic, Hilmija Popovec, and Dzamil Pezer.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not a Crisis Staff. Those were the leaders of the SDA party at the time. I think you know what is a Crisis Staff and what are party leaders. They did not take over power by force of arms as the Serb Crisis Staff did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the first day of your testimony, if I am not mistaken, you also mentioned the words "so-called Serbo-Croatian language." What do you mean? Was it not the official language throughout the existence of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a historian, you certainly know that that language was imposed with the creation of the first common state, the "common state." As soon as the former Yugoslavia collapsed, you couldn't say that you were speaking Croatian in Serbia or Serbian in Croatia, or anything else. It was called the Serbo-Croatian language; it is no where called by that name any longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not aware that in Serbia the Serbo-Croatian language had any negative implications.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that Ekavica was spoken in Serbia and Montenegro. Is the Ekavica dialect used throughout Serbia?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it is spoken in Serbia, Vojvodina, Sandzak. I mentioned that it was never spoken in Bosnia, and that is a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said it was also spoken in Montenegro. Is it spoken anywhere in Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned Senija Dzafic as an announcer and traitor in your written statement, which was tendered today, dated 1994. You also mentioned her husband. What ethnic group did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they fired from their job?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not because they placed themselves in the service. They found somebody who would read those lies on the radio, and they found her. That is my opinion, when I call her a traitor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is precisely what I wanted to refer to. Is a Muslim who was in favour of the survival of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Yugoslavia a traitor?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first it was only us Muslims who championed the survival of the former Yugoslavia. However, when we saw what the Serbian military were preparing for us, we were naturally against it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what was your attitude towards people who favoured, what I could call, a Serb option, the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war I respected the former state; I admit that and speak in sincerity. As soon as the war began, I started to hate them. I think you understand why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were certain changes in the media. You no longer listened to the Sarajevo media and that the area of Prijedor was limited to Belgrade media. Can I ask whether the Sarajevo media changed also? For example, the journal Novi Voks, have you ever heard of it, from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any changes in the Sarajevo media in that same period?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot judge. I always read Sarajevo papers; they were closer to me. Sometimes I read the Belgrade papers, like Ekspres Politika. I didn't go into the details of any changes. However, when the relay station on Mount Kozara was turned towards the Serb transmitters, when we started viewing only Serb programmes, when we started receiving only Serb press, Borba Ekspres Politika, I believe you will understand why I changed face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My learned friend Fila has already touched upon a question that I wanted to refer to, and that is the Muslim attack, or the resistance, as you call it. Let me just complete that part of the testimony relating to that chapter, if I may call it that. Do you know from what part of the city that resistance movement, if I can call it that, entered Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do. It came from the left bank of the Sana River, the area of Hambarine, Rizvanovici, Carakovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that close to Stari Grad, the old town?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not close -- yes, it is close. Yes. It depends on your viewpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in that conflict there were casualties?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I did not know. Later when I left the camp, I learnt who had been killed on either side. But at the time of the fighting, I didn't know, nor did it interest me at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume there were also wounded.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn from those stories, or can you tell us what it is you learnt, at least in broad lines, as to the number of dead, or a rough estimate for both sides?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't do that because that would just be guesswork.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To go back to your 1994 statement, in that statement, did you say that Slavko Ecim, a Croat, was the head of the resistance movement?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already explained what you mean by the resistance movement. But can you tell us whether you know whether, behind that resistance movement, there were any authorities behind it? And I'm thinking principally about the authorities from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they were. I think had they been the result would have been different. But I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Most of your written statement is devoted to the Ecimovic we mentioned. Did you know him well?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw him in Omarska, did you not?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that part of his life he spent as a paid worker in the Foreign Legion, a mercenary in the Foreign Legion?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Slavko Ecimovic, when there was a beating in Omarska, did he say, "I am an Ustasha"?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yes. Yes, and I say that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is the leader of that resistance movement.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the Ustashas were in World War II?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at the time all the Croats for you were Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm talking about what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That is why I'm saying that.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Omarska they said we and the Croats were Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this attempt to liberate Prijedor, did 10 to 15 per cent of former criminals take part in this, as you state in your 1994 statement?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think a part of them were, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that drive, did Mesic, nicknamed Hadzija, take part?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your written statement, did you say he was a renowned criminal?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say he was a renowned criminal, but I said that he had problems with the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I think that we can take a look at that statement which has been tendered into evidence, so there's no need to dwell on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, you don't want to take up the time of the Chamber, but I would like to know what all these details are telling us. I think that it is a very meandering way to arrive at Omarska, and perhaps a repetitive one, so if you could try to pay attention to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Hadzija, in May 1992, did he disarm the checkpoint at Berek?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the composition of the people at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in your written statement, did you not say that they were of a mixed composition?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The population of Berek, the old Stari Grad and Raskovac, asked that it be a mixed composition because it was inhabited predominantly by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he take the weapons away?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know about the attack on Kozarac. Do you know where the Kupovic [phoen] settlement is located?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about the incident that took place in that settlement prior to this attack?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only -- I didn't take part, I couldn't see it taking place, but I think that what happened was that fire was opened on a Serbian column going from Banja Luka. I think that was how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we're nearing Kozarac, from Omarska, when you were in Omarska, could you see for many days that it was looted and burnt?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that during the attack of the 24th of May, it was not completely destroyed?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot claim that. I cannot claim that. However, when I returned from Omarska to Trnopolje, we passed along the Banja Luka-Prijedor road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You came to Omarska, and if I'm correct, according to your statement, you said that when interrogated, when interviewed, you said you were a communist because the Serbs were communist too. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was a communist but I did not say that the Serbs were communist too. Of course they were; that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, your answer leads me to further questions. Was Radovan Karadzic ever a communist?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the SDS? Did it have anything in common with the communist orientation?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all former communists, all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are Chetniks akin to communists?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would appear to be so in this war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of a single Serb communist who was president of the former Yugoslavia, or prime minister?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, just like no Muslim was. I think the last time was in 1992. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in Omarska you spent most of your time on the pista, near the "white house".

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that you were able to see all the comings and goings very well?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you could hear voices.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Stojanovic, you asked the witness whether he was on the pista and whether he could see who was entering in and going out. You asked him that question. Why repeat that? Why are you repeating what the witness said? You keep repeating. If you have no questions, then move forward, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew Becir Medjunjanin.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not well. I knew his wife better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guards in Omarska, before the event that you started talking about when you were interviewed, show him up as an example to other prisoners? Did they make an example of him?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what sense?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Becir Medjunjanin was brought to the camp later on with his wife and his child, and I think he was captured in the Kozarac area. And when he arrived in the camp, all three of them had to stand up against the wall and were beaten, and then the guards would turn round and say, "This is the man who led Kozarac," and so on, things of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you. I should like to take up the story where Mr. Keegan left off, if I'm not mistaken, saying that he would return later on to that spot, but in fact he didn't go back to it. But if I'm not mistaken, I think you said that after a particular beating, that Becir Medjunjanin crawled to the door of your room in the "white house"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, and that is a well-known fact. I described the incident, the same day when Hankin was killed, and him too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We just want you to carry on with that description, because I don't think we have gone back to that event during the examination-in-chief. Could you tell us what happened after that to Becir, when he crawled to your door?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was beaten by Dusko Knezevic, nicknamed Duca. However, we were interested in what was going on in our own room at that particular point, what Zeljko Timarac did against a young man called Hankin, what he was doing to him. And when we returned from the "white house", when we had to run out onto the pista, I described Hankin's murder, how it came about. Soon after that, Becir Medjunjanin was taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the room, in the "white house" previously to that, did you sit next to Becir when Timarac and Duca came in and began beating him as you state in your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Becir Medjunjanin was in the first room of the "white house". When we came to the "white house", then afterwards Becir Medjunjanin was taken out by Dusko Knezevic. I gave a very clear statement to that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this statement did you say that in Omarska they would force you to watch other people being mistreated?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they wouldn't permit us to look, and I said that we secretly looked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, frankly, whether you know who killed Becir Medjunjanin?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. Dusko Knezevic, nicknamed Duca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he beat him with? Can you tell us in greater detail?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a baton, with his legs, with his arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this, did Becir fall down?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he stay immobile for some time?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He remained immobile for the rest of his life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them take him out?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see where they placed him?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the "white house", on the grass there, field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you notice any signs of life in him?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could note that there were no -- absolutely no signs of life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that at the same time when Hankin was a victim?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who killed Hankin?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zeljko Timarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to move to the events of (redacted) and Emir Beganovic. Can you remember, in your statement of 1994, what you said? Who beat them?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember. I said that they were beaten by Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask for the assistance of the technicians, and it is page 12 of the Serbian version and page 15 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the beginning of the page.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said page 12, did you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the first paragraph of page 12, in the Serbian version. "One afternoon, after I had been taken from the pista to the canteen ..." would you like to read it out?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain this to you. You probably want to know why I didn't mention Zigic's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that event very well, and that event was viewed by 600 people who were with me, in addition to myself. I know that I named Zigic, but why his name is not mentioned there, I don't want to enter into that. However, Zigic, Timarac, Dusko Knezevic is the group which, once or twice a week, would come to the Omarska camp and stay in the Omarska camp together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you see Zigic in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least ten times, and two or three times in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're just talking about Omarska for the time being. Thank you. Did you state that there were no other guards with them? That's what you say. You mentioned Timarac and Duca, and you expressly state that there were no other guards with him, and we're talking about -- there were no other guards presently with them?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you one thing, all the guards in the camp, in the Omarska camp, it was an attraction for them all when Zigic, Timarac, and Duca turned up, because they knew that at that time when they turned up, they would see something that they couldn't even see on film. And when it happened that Zigic beat Rezak or Began or anybody else, all the other guards from the surrounding points would come up to watch, to experience those incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you watching all this from?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the canteen, the menza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us on the model, please, where you were standing and where they were, that is to say, where Zigic was standing?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zigic, Duca came from this direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means they had already gone out, does it, from the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not in the "white house." They were somewhere behind here [indicates]. Where they actually were, I don't know. I was standing here [indicates]. Rezak was here. There was the dirty pool of water, and he washed himself with the dirty water in this area [indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was after that particular incident, was it?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was throughout -- it was all an incident for me. What do you mean "after"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you, in all your statements so far, you make no mention of the fact that Zigic took part in this incident. Can you tell us more specifically, in 1992, this incident took place. You gave your statements after two years. Now eight years later, you mention for the first time, as a new fact, as a novel fact compared to all your previous statements, that Zigic took part in that incident, in that occurrence.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What occurrence have you got in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The beating of (redacted) and Asaf Kapetanovic, and I think here is another – (redacted)

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I named Zigic. Why it wasn't entered into the records, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go through and look through all your statements?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did, but you know, after eight hours of interrogation, after interviewing, it was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Timarac take part in the incident as well?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he beat up these same people?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned in your statement that Timarac beat these people. Were you conscious of the fact that he would be responsible, perhaps, towards this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Timarac was present with Zigic on the pista when they came back all beaten up, and that is why I said that. You don't have to caution me at all. I know full well what statements I made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody caution you that your first statement was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I go back to my seat, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody caution you that your previous statements with respect to this incident were incorrect?

utterances.speaker: AZEDIN OKLOPCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
